While we acknowledge that studies—such as the 2018 evaluation of Chicago's bag tax by Homonoff et al.—demonstrate these fees can successfully reduce disposable bag usage and generate municipal revenue, these policies frequently place severe operational and financial burdens on stores. We are eager to discuss how the city can pursue its environmental objectives without disproportionately penalizing the local retail sector.
